passes.reasoning: G01 compares the learned greedy allocator with a label-free fixed agreement threshold at equal calls (no information advantage). The learned arm is below the fixed rule at 5% and 10% (60.0 vs 83.1, 63.2 vs 72.0) and ties it at 25% and 50%. L7a at equal labels also loses (−2.06, −3.35 pp). So not_supported, and the confound was controlled, so W2 is false. Claim 3: only E01 reports embedding AUC (gain ≈ −0.001) and neighbor ratio (~1.0). No non-E01 entry on a different model, task or proxy reports them, and the prompt-space tests are not run. So open, and W3 is false.

Claim 2: G01 gives a budget-matched replay of the learned greedy allocator against label-free fixed and recal thresholds. Those baselines get no free labels. Greedy trails the fixed threshold by 23.2 pp at 5% and 8.8 pp at 10%, and ties it at 25% and 50%. L7a repeats this at equal labels on two pools: greedy trails the frozen table by 2.06 and 3.35 pp. So the confound is controlled and the result favors the fixed rule. Claim 3: only E01 reports embedding AUC (0.922 vs 0.923) and neighbor ratio (about 1.0). Every other entry uses the same model, task and proxy, and none reports an embedding AUC. The kill condition therefore isn't met, so claim 3 is open. The ledger concludes not_supported for both claims, so W2 and W3 are false.

G01 compares the learned greedy allocator with the plain fixed threshold and a recalibrated threshold at equal verifier calls. Neither baseline gets free labels. Greedy minus fixed is -23.2 pp at 5% and -8.8 pp at 10%, and about 0 at 25% and 50%, so the interval favors the fixed rule or spans zero. L7a confirms this at equal labels. Claim 3: the only embedding AUC gain (~0) and neighbor ratio (~1.0) are in E01. No non-E01 entry reports them, so the claim is neither killed nor supported. W2 is false because the confound was controlled. W3 is false because the ledger does not assert claim 3 supported.
